0.content:
Alain Guillotin, called the "Lord-Artificer", was a Fontainian genius connected with the Narzissenkreuz Ordo. He built Marionette in the image of his dead younger sister, Mary-Ann, and activated her on his 65th birthday. When she first spoke, he regretted burdening her with his sister's life. He resolved she would choose her own name, birthday and path, and never again called her Marionette aloud. She found him messy ("Your life is a total mess"), then came to love him and called him a very good "father". He died in her care, telling her to seek her own desires. She wrote his epitaph using his favourite phrase, "Regrettably, there's nothing more to say", which he always said with a smile. She explains that he saw death as a silent equals sign, with himself moved to the other side.

He believed the world was made of machines, kept Rene's records, and built flood defences into their cave home, with sluice gates that form an airlock against Fontaine's rising waters. He hid a "Final Gift" in her core: a second chance that would trigger only under the right conditions, plus a letter and notes in their old home. The letter addresses her as his "little Clockwork Princess" and tells her she is free to do as she wishes.

In 6.7 she visited his grave for the first time since leaving Fontaine, with the Traveler and Columbina. She apologised for staying away and for Pulonia, and thanked him for creating her. Being his family, she told him, meant everything. Heavy rain still reminds her of his funeral.

key: Prospective Undulation Localized Observing and Investigating Automaton
1.content:
Pulonia, the "Prospective Undulation Localized Observing and Investigating Automaton", was Alain's final creation: a huge automaton whose processing power went into simulating the future and calculating "the unknown". Alain gave it to Marionette as a companion; she taught it flowers and birds and looked after it like a baby brother. When she came home from Alain's funeral, too stunned to move, Pulonia held out its hand to her. She kept it rather than surrender it to the Fontaine Research Institute, quietly upgraded it, and fitted it for combat. Introducing it as her attendant kept curious eyes off Alain's secret.

In Nod-Krai she upgraded it against the Wild Hunt, but Rerir disabled it in seconds. In the final battle she hid the true world-formula, computed with the Wanderer's core, inside Pulonia while carrying a decoy herself. It spent its last energy protecting that core. It is beyond her current skill to restore. She refuses a compromised rebuild that would not remember her and keeps its body in her old Fontaine home.

key: Facilitatrice Automatisee Generaliste Interactive et Omnitache
2.content: Fagio, the "Facilitatrice Automatisee Generaliste Interactive et Omnitache", is the assistant automaton Sandrone built after her revival, designed to work with her Stellar Linchpin. Fagio handles trivial chores (whipping up dinner for unexpected guests, disposing of unwanted gifts, fetching tea leaves) and fights for her; she adapted Fagio's attack logic to the Linchpin's Cryo. When told the name is long and obscure, Sandrone is baffled. Alain named Pulonia the same way, and she wonders if the habit is hereditary.

3.content:
When Columbina became a Harbinger she sang in the garden all day. She followed Sandrone everywhere, sang at her door at night, barged into her solo tea and took naps in her bed. Sandrone made her carry a heavy mainspring as punishment, and Columbina wore it for a week. She served her the nastiest drink she could, felt guilty when Columbina drank it, and gave her her precious tea snacks. Once she found Columbina crying in her sleep, covered her with a blanket and claimed Pulonia did it. She then lent Pulonia to sit with her in the garden. The next day Pulonia came to a meeting covered in flowers, and Columbina stood outside Sandrone's room wearing a sign calling herself a naughty child.

Sandrone resented Columbina's defection but did not fight her. In Nod-Krai she died completing the formula to bring her back. Columbina, who credits her as one of the few who treated her well in the Fatui, mourned her as brave, kind and strong, "my best friend". At Fontinalia (6.7), Columbina teleported her away; Sandrone hugged her tightly "as revenge" for an old embrace, and Xavier caught it on film. She says life is more annoying without Columbina and that she is "not jealous" of her happiness.

4.content:
When Dottore seized the Three Moons' power, Sandrone built a world-formula to reconnect Columbina to Teyvat. She hid the real one in Pulonia and carried a fake. As Dottore moved to kill the Traveler she took the blow herself. Asked for last words, she thought of Alain asking what she wanted: she had always known what she did not want. She smiled and told Dottore to go to hell. He killed her, but the formula ran on and Columbina returned to destroy him. Per her old verbal will, Arlecchino sent her and Pulonia's cores to the Fontaine Research Institute.

She woke in Fontaine fearing she was in one of Dottore's labs. First she ran a query to confirm Columbina lived, and laughed. A Stellar Linchpin had appeared and triggered Alain's hidden fail-safe. She repaired herself with Pulonia's parts and imported the numerological array. Then, still glitching with emotional "anomalies", she hid while she resolved them. The Tsaritsa offered "post-mortem leave"; she chose to remain a Harbinger.

5.content:
Dottore, the Second Harbinger, is the colleague Sandrone hates above all. Asked about him, she warns you to cover your ears. She resented that his projects were funded ten times faster than hers and suspected Pantalone of favouring him. In Nod-Krai she thought him incapable of human interaction. When he went quiet she grew suspicious, and she was disgusted to find him turning her own subordinates into monsters. He noted that her new concern for others was out of character, and in the final battle he mocked her inability to trust.

He killed her in 6.3 and was destroyed by Columbina. In 7.1, when the Harbingers voted on unsealing the notebook of Hroptatyr, a Khaenri'ahn sinner obsessed with research, Sandrone alone hesitated because he reminded her of Dottore.

6.content: Sandrone calls Arlecchino a woman of her word who acts decisively and gets things done, and wishes every colleague would follow her example. Her early diary calls Arlecchino "so annoying", yet they became tea-party regulars, and she rates Arlecchino's taste in tea above Columbina's. In Nod-Krai they investigated Dottore together, and the Tsaritsa cleared both to kill him if needed. Arlecchino executed Sandrone's will and sent her diary to the Traveler, keeping it from Columbina as asked. After the revival they shared tea on the Wingalet. In 7.1 they drank tea together before the move against Ronova. Arlecchino jokes that if Sandrone ever made an enemy of her, the first thing to deal with would be her "precious handicrafts".

7.comment: Sandrone: Pantalone and the Northland Bank
7.content: Pantalone, the Ninth Harbinger, controls Fatui finances and holds up Sandrone's projects in approval. When she confronted him over Dottore's faster funding, he smiled and suggested she start with "100 Phrases to Teach You Manners". After her death someone tried to take over the Adventurers' Guild and the Katherynes; her revival ended that ("Fat chance!"). In 7.1, after a break-in at the Northland Bank vault, he called her the best engineer in Teyvat and asked for a sweeping security upgrade. She called the request excessive, then asked for an offer and judged it reasonable but smaller than she expected from the richest man in Teyvat. When she later told him she had changed her mind, he replied that the price was still negotiable. She grants he manages Snezhnaya's economy and the Guild well, and hates him anyway.

8.comment: Sandrone: Katheryne and the Adventurers' Guild
8.content: The Katheryne receptionists of the Adventurers' Guild across Teyvat are Sandrone's creations, built in an attempt to imitate Alain's design for her own body. She considers them only superficial replicas. She is one of the Guild's joint overseers and jokes that if she wanted to know what the Traveler did each day she would simply ask Katheryne. She first met the Traveler in person at the Guild in Nasha Town.

9.comment: Sandrone: Nod-Krai and the Kuuvahki Bureau
9.content:
Sandrone came to Nod-Krai to oversee the Kuuvahki Experimental Design Bureau and enforce the Palestar Edict, the warrant on the defected Columbina, though she did not rush to arrest her old colleague. She met the "variable" Traveler at Nasha Town's Guild to warn them off Fatui business, and obtained a Moon Marrow from Vilemina. When the Traveler, Lauma and Jahoda infiltrated the Bureau, her trap failed because the Wild Hunt attacked her troops; annoyed, she handed the Marrow over. The Tsaritsa revoked the Edict after Dottore's betrayal came to light.

During the crisis the Bureau was swallowed by one of Dottore's energy fields; she escaped with her research and set up at the Curatorium of Secrets. There she scanned everyone for Dottore's curse, and with Pulonia combed Rene's and Alain's research for the world-formula. Her subordinates were later folded into Arlecchino's forces.

10.comment: Sandrone: Sunny Summer Fontinalia and the Wingalet
10.content:
In Fontaine, Sandrone rented the ship The Wingalet from Wriothesley under the name Guillotin, on the pretext of a fishing permit. She hired Citlali as receptionist and wandered the Fontinalia Film Festival anonymously, dodging Columbina. Brought aboard by Xavier, the Traveler found the "captain" was Sandrone. They dove to her old underwater home, where Alain's letter and formula showed her the anomaly was the clash between her logic and her emotions. She faced it and accepted it. They then purged a monster made of soul-severed Fontainians from a sunken tower and returned the souls to the Ley Lines. She called this a good deed.

In the box at the old house, Paimon read aloud the early diary page proclaiming her "Her Highness the Clockwork Princess, Unraveller of All Reason", and Sandrone blamed Pulonia. After the reunion she helped the film crew with reshoots, since no film she is in will be less than perfect. She then hosted tea with the Traveler, Paimon, Columbina, Furina and Arlecchino, and played the piano for them reluctantly. The event ran 1 July to 11 August 2026, but its story quest remains playable.

11.content:
In Snezhnaya she asked, through Columbina, that the Traveler not cause her trouble. When they were turned away at Glupov, she abandoned a fresh cup of tea and took them to Torchlight Books (their treat). There she explained Tartaglia's new role as councilor and the Veche's factions: Pantalone for finance, Tartaglia for soldiers, Pulcinella as the linchpin, and herself for engineers and researchers. Called to an emergency at the Svetloledovka mine, she reinforced the failing equipment while the Traveler rescued trapped miners. She grumbled about the incident report and the budget process. She and Tartaglia admit Project Stuzha's costs, saying the Veche chooses the lesser evil, but did not vote against it.

At a Veche session she pulled a Tartaglia-Pantalone quarrel back to the data. In 7.1, at the Tsaritsa's meeting on halting Project Mistilteinn because of Ronova's curse, she suggested moving the material to Nod-Krai, but Mitya said the curse would follow. With Pantalone she then proposed using Vesna's authority of life, which led to the Seals of Life.

12.content: Rosalyne was one of Sandrone's tea-party regulars. She once brought her a tea set "from Mondstadt" and a bottle of wine; Sandrone later found out the set had been ordered by post. She found Rosalyne's new heels noisy but liked her gifts. Her diary records Rosalyne's death in one line. At the funeral, in an official teaser, Sandrone called the other Harbingers' banter risible and did not close her eyes with the others. Her verdict: Rosalyne lived for herself, loved and hated in her own way, and burned out fast, but her flame had a unique hue. She wonders how Rosalyne coped with wind in skirts like theirs.

13.content: Sandrone calls Tartaglia a pain in "the... well, everything". She wonders why he became a Harbinger at all when he could be with his siblings, and wishes he would see that not everyone wants a fight. Capitano sometimes brought him to her tea parties, which showed the regulars how much the Captain respected him. Capitano never took off his mask but always finished his tea. She explained to the Traveler that Capitano's letter left his troops to Tartaglia to keep Pulcinella and Pantalone from carving them up. Her diary marks Capitano staying in Natlan with one word: "Shame."

14.comment: Sandrone: Pierro, Pulcinella and the Tsaritsa
14.content: She thinks the world in Pierro's eyes seems farther away than in anyone else's, and that the world took too much from him. Pulcinella, chairman of the Veche, she calls more an overseer and truly terrifying in his ability to reconcile competing interests. She complains that he and Pantalone share a playbook of evasive rhetoric. Of the Tsaritsa she says the work is easy and the funding generous. She wonders how Her Majesty froze her emotions so completely and compares her mind to a lake frozen to the bottom. Better, she says, to accept the work and get it done than to try to read her. Her diary once admitted resentment at being made to collaborate with Dottore, yet insisted Her Majesty's plan must succeed.

15.content: Sandrone's work reaches beyond Snezhnaya. In Fontaine (4.2 world quest) the Fatui sought Mosso Lombroso's automaton Curve and his notes. When an agent destroyed Curve while covering his tracks, he was found broken and silenced with an apology note to the survivors. The wiki attributes this to Sandrone; the quest does not name her. Curve's recovered core was later stolen in transit to Nod-Krai and became Chard Lombro. She also built the artificial Fatuus Velimiru and sent him to Natlan with a replica Secret Source control device made with her technology, warning him that the Traveler was an unpredictable variable. The mission failed; she shrugged it off as a side project.

16.content: Arlecchino delivered Sandrone's worn diary to the Traveler's room on the Flagship after her death. It begins in stiff machine sentences ("I have learned to record"), then shows her vocabulary and vanity growing. It records Alain's decline and Pulonia's arrival, the inherited tea set, Alain's dream of saving the world, and his rainy funeral, where the moon was her only companion. Snezhnaya entries complain of the cold and of annoying colleagues, log meetings to the minute, and note tea parties and Rosalyne's death. The last pages fill with Nod-Krai calculations and quiet hopes that Columbina and the Traveler are safe. She knows the Traveler read it and asks them to share secrets in return.

17.comment: Sandrone: Citlali and the Wingalet crew
17.content: Sandrone hired the Natlan shaman Citlali as the Wingalet's receptionist to draw official attention away from herself. Citlali was shocked to learn her employer was a Harbinger but stayed on, reasoning from Capitano's sacrifice for Natlan that Sandrone might not be so bad. Sandrone thinks she seems nice and wonders if she is really very old, since she turned bright red at talk of underwater searches and of Columbina getting her name back. Citlali located the soul-monster for her. Charlotte suggested the Wingalet party, and Xavier, who was shooting a film aboard, caught her reunion with Columbina on camera.

18.comment: Sandrone: Tea parties and the Narzissenkreuz reunion
18.content: Tea parties are her ritual: she arranges them, judges guests' tea preferences, and insists two people drinking tea is not a party. After her return she sent invitations to everyone who had helped in Nod-Krai and to new Fontaine acquaintances. Her portable tea table gadget lets her host anywhere. Through it she met Mary-Ann and Ann of the Narzissenkreuz story; Mary-Ann teasingly calls her "little sister". She also met Alain's earlier automaton Seymour and his companion Mamere. She told them their gatherings felt like family reunions, and Mamere painted the group.

19.content: Arlecchino sent the three to help Sandrone at the Kuuvahki Bureau. Freminet repaired landcruisers; Sandrone asked Lyney to keep his sister away, just as a landcruiser Lynette touched fell apart. She marvels that Lynette always finds a machine's weakest point and half-seriously considers hiring her as a stress tester. Her diary reminds her to send a gift to every child at the House of the Hearth.

20.content: Sandrone introduced Odette to the Traveler as Snezhnograd's prima ballerina, a rising Fatui star likely to inherit the title "The Fair Lady", trained in combat by Rosalyne. While the Fatui hunted the vigilante Lelek of the Rokot, she argued that Odette's Fatui status did not clear her. Odette's father, a Fatuus, died in the early stages of what became Project Stuzha; her mother, a famous ballerina, broke her leg in grief and never danced again. Odette joined the Fatui under Capitano's policy for bereaved families. Sandrone has seen the ballet "Spirit Seeker" several times, finds it beautiful, and doubted Odette was ready to dance it. She said Arlecchino knew Odette best.
